items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And we were staying together in the loft on Broadway, 89 E Broadway Street.

ctx.x: Kiwami. K-I-N-I-B-I [misspelled] Ziwati. And we were staying together in the loft on Broadway, 89 E Broadway Street. And all kinds of people would come by and sessions, and we studied, actually we were vegetarians at the time. And so he called Kiwami to come in and play for a few gigs and whatnot, and Sun Ra asked Kiwami did he know of a saxophone player. So Kiwami recommended me, because Pharoah had went with — Pharoah was doing presentations and performances with Sun Ra as well, but he had worked with Trane.…

from Alabama basically, by way of Chicago. So I didn’t really eat that much because I was so excited about playing with the group that I’d never played that way before. I’d never played that free style before you know. So when I started playing he told me to forget about changes, just think about the sound and imagery you know. Let your imagination take control.
